title: Development Impact Guest Blogger | Guest bloggers
gist: An index page listing roughly 280 Development Impact guest-post titles; it has no argument of its own but the titles reveal recurring research themes: women's labor force participation in India, technology adoption in agriculture, state capacity and taxation, and RCT methodology.

insights.claim: A dominant cluster of recent development-economics research examines why women stay out of work in South Asia, citing household bargaining, spousal jealousy, safety, childcare and commuting frictions.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Female labor supply remains a key untapped growth lever in India; watch policies addressing childcare and safe transit.
insights.quote: Expecting the worst: Household bargaining and the suppression of women’s work in India.

insights.claim: Guest posts report that even limited childcare can transform family labor and that mothers-in-law sharing housework raise women's labor force participation.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Childcare provision is a cheap lever for labor supply growth in emerging markets.
insights.quote: Scaling short days: Even limited childcare can transform family labor.

insights.claim: Recurring research topics include barriers to agricultural technology adoption, such as knowledge hoarding, risk, information frictions and mechanization access via digital monitoring.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Adoption frictions, not just technology availability, cap agtech uptake in developing markets.
insights.quote: When sharing is not caring: Knowledge Hoarding as a Barrier to Agricultural Innovation.

insights.claim: One featured study argues price controls spread technology but stall innovation.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Price-controlled markets may see diffusion but weak product innovation, relevant to regulated sectors.
insights.quote: Priced for Development? How Price Controls Spread Technology but Stall Innovation

insights.claim: Guest posts repeatedly study state capacity, including whether low capacity caps tax rates in D.R. Congo, wealth taxation in developing countries, and algorithmic tax assessment improving equity.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Tax-capacity constraints shape fiscal outlooks in frontier economies.
insights.locator: Does Low State Capacity Set a Ceiling

insights.claim: One study title reports that adopting an algorithm improves tax equity when bureaucrats undervalue the wealth of the richest.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Algorithmic property/tax assessment is a govtech opportunity.
insights.quote: Adopting an algorithm improves tax equity when bureaucrats undervalue the wealth of the richest.
insights.locator: Adopting an algorithm improves tax equity

insights.claim: The blog hosts methodological debates such as correct attrition testing, index construction, Bayesian meta-analysis, and how well impact evaluations generalize across 600 papers on 20 intervention types.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Evidence external validity is limited; be cautious extrapolating single-study results.
insights.quote: What do 600 papers on 20 types of interventions tell us about how much impact evaluations generalize?
